coupled_example.error: joint does not factorise (max deviation 6.800e-04 > tol 1.0e-12); refusing to project onto marginals

grid.unit: distinct table row, non-no_answer entry, one at a time
grid.renormalisation: Perturbed entry clipped, remaining entries rescaled so the row sums to 1

diagnosis.reading: The three questions' mean IGs span 0.0250 bits, while a single +/-0.05 perturbation of one entry moves one question's mean IG by up to 0.0341 bits. The ordering test was asking the sweep to resolve a signal smaller than its own step size, so the flips are decisive re-orderings rather than fourth-decimal ties: 9 of 11 flips at +/-0.05 leave the new winner ahead by more than 0.002 bits.
diagnosis.grid_limitation: The grid was pre-registered in absolute probability units and never checked against the spread of the quantity being ordered. An absolute 0.10 is 14% of a 0.70 entry and 100% of a 0.10 entry, so one grid is a mild and a total perturbation depending on where it lands. Same shape of blind spot as the Gate 2 count threshold that was not scale-free. The grid is NOT changed and the sweep is NOT re-run on a different one: §5 pre-registered this decision rule and repairing the test after seeing it fail is the thing pre-registration exists to prevent.

sweep.verdict: answer model too fragile to illustrate anything: the ordering flips under a +/-0.05 perturbation, so the illustration is withdrawn rather than repaired by choosing better entries
sweep.measures: stability of the information-gain magnitudes (the mechanism)
sweep.does_not_measure: the impossibility result, which is answer-model-free and cannot be defended or undermined by this sweep
